text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 401s for /api/v1/session/verify across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Source: auth-provider (Auth0) upstream certificate rotation errors. Paging on-call SRE.

sre-oncall: seeing +900 401s in last 5m, login failures and console 403s. Traces point to token signature verification failing with `kid not found` and `x5c chain invalid`.

eng-oncall: joining. are we getting any 5xxs or just 401/403s? which flows affected (user logins, machine-to-machine)?

sre-oncall: primarily interactive user logins and console sessions. Some service-to-service calls using client credentials also failing to validate.

alex (console): users reporting console "access denied" when clicking sign-in. Holding on customer calls. Can we expect a fix soon?

jordan (security): likely Auth0 rotated cert chain and pushed a new key set before our JWKS cache refreshed. We have fallback logic but it seems to reject malformed x5c entries.

lee (infra): confirmed our JWKS fetch healthchecks show increased 5xx from auth-provider; cached JWKS TTL is 60s currently. We can increase TTL to 600s as emergency to avoid repeated fetch attempts and rely on cached keys short-term.

maria (oncall): taking lead for mitigation. plan: 1) increase JWKS TTL 2) enable signature-verification fallback to accept previously cached keys for 10m 3) route console auth through dedicated fallback region where keys still valid. Anyone object?

eng-oncall: ok to deploy TTL bump and fallback verification change. I'll push a canary to us-west-2 first.

sre-oncall: deploy commands below (will run with rollback window).

```
# emergency: increase JWKS cache ttl
kubectl -n platform patch cm auth-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"jwks_cache_ttl":"600"}}'
# enable legacy-key-accept
kubectl -n platform patch cm auth-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"accept_cached_jwks":"true"}}'
```

ops-bot: Deploy job started: auth-service/config-patch v.urgent/2285123456 -> canary us-west-2.

eng-oncall: canary applied, monitoring logs.

sre-oncall: immediate drop in JWKS fetch errors, 401 rate is trending down from peak. Console requests still failing for a subset of users — looks like their tokens were minted with new key that our cache no longer has and their clients can't refresh.

sam (support): CS is getting back to affected customers with a short note. Important to include ETA and workaround (clear local SSO cookies / re-run login flow). Preparing a status page update.

product-ops: please post to status: "We are investigating authentication errors affecting some users in US/EU regions. Mitigation in progress; temporary increased authentication cache in place to reduce errors."

alex (console): can we add an interim UI notice for console login that prompts users to retry? I can push a small banner via feature toggle.

eng-oncall: banner pushed (feature-toggle: auth_retry_banner). Also adding server-side retry for token introspect with short backoff.

sre-oncall: after TTL bump + fallback, 401s reduced by ~78% over 10m. But still seeing ~5% residual failures concentrated on older mobile clients that pin tokens longer. Next step: trigger reissue flow for sessions older than 24h — force soft-refresh.

jordan (security): agree with soft-refresh. need to avoid creating open redirect or session fixation. Use existing refresh endpoint flow only.

maria (oncall): scheduling handoff to next oncall in 45m. @lee please confirm we have telemetry dashboards recording per-customer impact for post-incident review.

lee (infra): creating dashboard: `auth0_rotation_incident/2285123456` with per-customer 401s, token_age distribution, and jwks_fetch_errors.

ops-bot: Alert suppressed temporarily: auth-provider error threshold muted for 30m while mitigation stabilizes.

product-ops: status page update posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2285123456

sam (support): Customer impact snapshot for comms: ~2.1k unique users affected, ~47 tenants with >10 reported failures, most errors between 2023-11-03T14:22Z and 2023-11-03T15:05Z in dataplane regions us-west-2, eu-west-1. Drafting email for tiered customers.

maria (oncall): handoff note: mitigation applied (JWKS TTL increased, cached-key fallback enabled, console banner live). Residual impact on legacy mobile clients; support notified. Next oncall: continue monitoring, coordinate with Auth0 support for root cause and key rotation timeline.

eng-oncall: filing CHER (change) to revert TTL/fallback after Auth0 confirms stable keyset and we validate new x5c entries: CHG-2285123456-revert.

jordan (security): postmortem checklist: capture JWKS payloads before/after rotation, timeline of when keys observed to change, why our client rejected x5c chain, test suite update to simulate malformed x5c. Assign to eng-ml? no, eng-security.

sre-oncall: marking this thread as incident-live. Will update with final numbers after 24h.

incident-bot: Incident created #INC-2285123456, priority P1 -> P2 after mitigation. Oncall handoff scheduled to maria in 45m.

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll leave a short playbook in the ticket for future rotations: 1) prefetch new JWKS 2) stagger TTL reductions 3) notify platform 30m before rotation if vendor supports it. Closing active paging; keep channel open for updates.

sam (support): sending customer-facing summary to top tenants now.

lee (infra): logs + dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/auth0-rotation-2285123456

eng-oncall: CHG and rollback plan created. If anything regresses, re-open page.

sre-oncall: last check: 401s back to baseline. moving to monitoring. thanks all :thumbsup:
